results.why: Deck B is a recognizable Jeskai Control shell. It runs full playsets of No More Lies and Lightning Helix alongside Get Lost and Three Steps Ahead, and 26 lands fit its curve. Deck A fields 27 lands plus 4 near-unplayed Tablets of Discovery, which is far too much mana, and it skips Get Lost and Three Steps for weaker cards like Sear and Firebending Lesson. A's Flashback and North Wind Avatar are also odd picks.

Deck A is the established Jeskai Control shell. It runs Get Lost, Three Steps Ahead, a full set of No More Lies and Lightning Helix, and Resonating Lute to power out Revelations, with a sensible 26-land base. Deck B drops the core cheap interaction (no Get Lost or Three Steps, only two No More Lies) in favor of fringe picks like Tablet of Discovery and Firebending Lesson, which is out of place outside a Lessons deck. That makes B's early game and counter suite notably weaker.

Deck B is a coherent dork-ramp shell, with Llanowar Elves, Gene Pollinator, Spider Manifestation and Bloom Tender feeding Nature's Rhythm into Ouroboroid and Craterhoof Behemoth. Its 20 lands plus about 15 mana creatures are reasonable, and it has red sources for the Balloon Man. Deck A mixes prowess pieces (Stormchaser's Talent, Boomerang Basics) into a Bant creature deck with few payoffs, plays Nature's Rhythm with weak targets, and runs Jolly Balloon Man with no red mana.

Deck A is a coherent green ramp shell: Llanowar Elves, Gene Pollinator, Bloom Tender and Spider Manifestation feed Nature's Rhythm, Ouroboroid and Craterhoof. Its many dual and any-color sources cover the splashes for Gearhulk, Seam Rip and Balloon Man. Deck B mashes prowess pieces (Stormchaser's Talent, Boomerang Basics) into a creature deck with almost no dorks for Badgermole Cub and no real red source for Balloon Man, and it lists 61 cards.

Deck B pairs its Dwarf-equipment core with real interaction in Burst Lightning and Shock. It also runs efficient payoffs: Hard-Won Jitte double strike with cheap Mauler equips, Spider-Suit, and Dáin Ironfoot granting double strike. Deck A plays no removal and carries clunky pieces like Doc Ock's Tentacles with no 5-drops to trigger it, plus Leyline Axe and Collar filler, so it is a less coherent and less resilient list.

Deck A runs the same Dwarf/Equipment core but adds seven cheap burn spells for interaction and payoffs like Hard-Won Jitte, Dáin Ironfoot and Mjölnir, which turn cheap equips into lethal double strike. It does this on a sensible 18-land base. Deck B plays 23 lands in a deck curving out at four, has zero interaction, and wastes slots on off-tribe Raubahn and clunky Doc Ock's Tentacles, so it will flood and lose to opposing threats.

Deck B is a coherent mono-black aristocrats shell with clean mana. It recurs sacrifice fodder through Bloodghast, Forsaken Miner (its crimes come from Hex, Sheriff and the targeted drains of Egotist and Sackville) and Nine-Lives Familiar, and turns every sacrifice into drain with real removal. Deck A stretches three colors over 21 lands to run four Biotech Specialists with thin synergy, so it is clunkier and less consistent.

Deck A is a coherent mono-black aristocrats shell with perfect mana. Recursive fodder (Bloodghast, Forsaken Miner, Nine-Lives Familiar) feeds a free sac outlet in Umbral Collar Zealot and drain payoffs in Popular Egotist and Sackville, and those targeted triggers also count as crimes that rebuy Miner. Deck B stretches into a third color mostly for the mediocre Biotech Specialist and runs off-plan cards like Gene Pollinator, so its manabase and focus are worse despite Rottenmouth Viper's power.

Deck B has a cleaner Boros superfriends shell. It backs the walkers with efficient, proven removal (Burst Lightning, Get Lost, Sear, Helix), and Voice of Victory protects them during your turn. Its 24-land mana base is all dual or basic and supports both RR and WW, while Deck A runs five colorless or awkward lands (Fountainport, Sunken Citadel) and filler like Caretaker's Talent, The Mind Stone and Cori Mountain Monastery that weakens a color-hungry walker deck.

Deck A is a cleaner superfriends shell. It runs 17 planeswalkers backed by efficient, flexible removal (Burst Lightning, Get Lost, Helix, Sear) and Voice of Victory to protect its turns. Its mana is all dual-colour or basics, which suits the WW and RR costs. Deck B dilutes the plan with Way of the Pyromancer, Mind Stone and Iceberg, and strains its mana with colorless Fountainports, tapped Citadels and Cori Monastery, so it lacks the consistency and interaction density of A.

Deck B is much closer to real Mono-Green Devotion, with Ouroboroid, Kiora and Outcaster Trailblazer as its engine. Those cards draw off big creatures and keep the ramp from running out of gas, and Boseiju adds useful interaction. Deck A leans on clunky top-end like Emrakul (which barely gets cheaper in a mono-creature deck), Summon: Bahamut and Titan with little card flow, so its plan is less consistent.

Deck A runs the real engine cards of the archetype: Ouroboroid, Kiora and Outcaster Trailblazer give it a strong midgame and card flow. Ouroboroid also turns on Fight Rigging and The Great Henge reliably. Deck B leans on clunky top-end like Emrakul (few card types in the graveyard), a 9-mana Bahamut and Invasion of Ikoria, and lacks Ouroboroid, so it is slower and less consistent.

Deck B is a coherent mono-white heroic shell. It runs 18 creatures with real heroic payoffs (Phalanx Leader, Hero of Iroas) and enough protection (Gods Willing, Feat of Resistance, Sejiri Shelter) to keep its targets alive against removal-heavy Pioneer, all on clean mana with Mutavault and Eiganjo. Deck A runs only 14 creatures, including the odd Speedball, plays no protection spells for a heroic deck, and spends slots on filler like Academic Dispute without Lessons, all while paying painland and Confluence life.

Deck A is a coherent mono-white heroic list with clean mana, more threats (18 creatures plus Mutavault) and real protection in Gods Willing, Feat of Resistance, Sejiri Shelter, Sheltered by Ghosts and Hallowblade. That protection is what makes a targeting deck work through removal. Deck B has stronger individual cards in Swiftspear and Monstrous Rage, but it runs only 14 creatures, nearly no protection, and filler like Academic Dispute, Practiced Offense and Speedball, so it folds to a single removal spell.

Deck B adds real control tools to the Jeskai Revelation shell: No More Lies, Supreme Verdict, Get Lost, Sear and The Wandering Emperor. Deck A instead leans on narrow Fiery Impulse, Erode and a clunky Together as One, with no countermagic. B's manabase is a bit tapped-heavy, but its triomes and shocks give more reliable black for Inevitable Defeat, so B's plan holds together better overall.

Deck A pairs the Revelation and Defeat top end with a proven UW Control shell: No More Lies, Get Lost, Supreme Verdict and The Wandering Emperor. That gives it real answers to opposing spells and a 4-mana sweeper rather than a 6-mana one. Deck B has no counterspells and leans on Fiery Impulse and Erode, which struggle against bigger threats. Its Farewell and Together as One make an already top-heavy curve worse, while A's three-colour-plus-splash mana is comparably sound.

Deck B is a coherent Izzet Terror/Crab shell. It has cheap cantrips to fuel the cost reductions and a real interaction suite: Fiery Impulse, Burst Lightning, Lightning Axe, Traumatic Critique and Spell Pierce. Its mana supports a light green splash for Bushwhack. Deck A has almost no removal beyond bounce and a fight spell, and it spends slots on clunky Simic filler like Cache Grab, Analyze the Pollen and Up the Beanstalk, so it can't handle opposing threats.

Deck A is a coherent Temur tempo shell. Cheap cantrips fuel Crab and Terror, and it packs real interaction (Fiery Impulse, Burst Lightning, Lightning Axe, Spell Pierce, Critique), with a mana base that supports the green splash for Bushwhack. Deck B has almost no removal beyond Bushwhack fights and bounce, and cards like Cache Grab and Analyze the Pollen are weak filler, so it would struggle against faster aggro and combo decks.

Deck B is a coherent Rakdos Persist/reanimator shell with real enablers: Faithless Looting, Bloodghast, Village Rites, Corrupted Conviction, and Fatal Push and Bolt for interaction. Its mana is sound for a two-color deck. Deck A is mono-black with few ways to discard Archon besides Street Wraith and Eyetwitch, and it plays filler like Poet's Quill and an off-color Overgrown Tomb, so its plan is far less consistent.

Deck A keeps the core engine of real Persist lists: Faithless Looting, Eyetwitch and sac-to-draw spells to bin Archon, Persist to return it, plus Fatal Push, Bolt and Bowmasters as cheap interaction on a clean Rakdos manabase. Deck B relies on random mills from Overlord and Supplier to find Archon, has almost no direct discard outlets, and runs only a few interaction spells. Its manabase also includes Overgrown Tomb and Underground Mortuary with no green cards, so B's plan is less reliable.

Deck B is built on the proven Eldrazi Ramp shell: Utopia Sprawl, Talisman of Impulse and Delighted Halfling feed Eldrazi Temple payoffs, with Sire and Devourer as top-end that is castable and interacts. Its 9 Forests reliably support Sprawl, and Turntimber adds land count without costing spell slots. Deck A runs four clunky Emrakul plus Ulamog off only 18 real lands and a fragile Fanatic/GSZ engine. It also lacks Devourer and Sire and has a shakier green and colorless balance, so it is less consistent.

Deck B ties the Trudge plan together: Fanatic of Rhonas turns on with Trudge for four mana, Green Sun's Zenith tutors either piece, and Mosswort Bridge, Fight Rigging and Disciple all reward a big body. Its top end of Ugin, Ulamog and four Emrakul is stronger, and the land-MDFCs give it enough mana sources. Deck A has more raw ramp, but it runs 61 cards and only a thin, weak top end of Sire, Devourer and three Emrakul, with no Ugin. Seven-mana Turntimber Symbiosis is a clunky enabler next to Zenith.

Deck B is a coherent UB storm shell: Dark Ritual, LED, Infernal Tutor and Brainstorm feed Tendrils, Thoughtseize protects the combo, and 13 lands with fetches, duals and artifact lands support both colors. Deck A has only two Volcanic Islands plus two MDFCs for blue and red, yet runs black Ovalchase Daredevils with no black lands. Its single Grapeshot kill backed by Gamble and Does Machines is far less reliable.

Deck A is a coherent Ub storm list. Dark Ritual, LED, Infernal Tutor and Brainstorm assemble Tendrils, Riddlesmith and the Baubles add an artifact-draw engine, and the mana is well supported by duals and fetches. Deck B's mana is a mess: only 2 Volcanic Islands plus 2 MDFCs for colored mana alongside Ancient Tomb and Urza's Saga, no black land for Ovalchase Daredevil, and a pile of slow Class enchantments built around a single Grapeshot.

Deck B is a coherent Phoenix engine: Faithless Looting and Buried Alive bin Phoenixes, and free or cheap spells like Gut Shot, Mutagenic Growth and Lava Dart (with flashback) make three instants or sorceries in a turn easy to reach. Deck A has the same core but fewer cheap triggers and spends slots on off-plan cards like The Fantasticar, Daze and Thoughtseize. Its red base is also thinner for a Phoenix deck, so its plan hangs together worse.

Both decks run the same core engine: Dark Ritual into Buried Alive, then a third instant or sorcery to bring Phoenixes back on turn one. Deck B backs that engine with Thoughtseize and Daze to protect the combo, and runs a leaner 15-land manabase with 4 Lotus Petal. Deck A spends slots on weak filler like Mutagenic Growth (often no creature to target), Gut Shot and Lava Dart, and runs 18 lands, which dilutes a fast combo deck.

Deck B is a coherent Boros artifact-aggro shell with real interaction: Bolt, Galvanic Blast, Journey and Thraben Charm, plus Skyfisher and Glint Hawk value engines. Its 18 lands, including artifact lands, support both metalcraft and its colors. Deck A has no removal or interaction at all, plays filler like Phyrexian Walker and Ornithopter, and runs only 14 lands, so it would fold to any blocker or sweeper.

Deck A is a coherent Boros artifact-aggro shell. It has real interaction in Bolt, Galvanic Blast, Journey and Thraben Charm, plus genuine synergy between Glint Hawk, Kor Skyfisher and its artifact lands, on a reasonable 18-land base. Deck B leans on filler like Phyrexian Walker and Ornithopter to go wide with no removal at all, and it skips staples like Kor Skyfisher, Thraben Charm and Prismatic Strands, so it can't handle opposing threats or blockers.

Deck A has a real, focused kill: Tireless Tribe pumps its toughness by discarding, Inside Out swaps power and toughness, and Escape Tunnel or Fling finishes. It also runs a full looting and draw package that feeds discard while recurring Sneaky Snacker and the Eidolons. Deck B is a fair Boros pile of low-impact creatures like Boros Recruit, Wojek Halberdiers and the clunky 4-mana Eidolons, and it lacks the card quality to beat Pauper's top decks.

Deck A is a coherent Boros aggro list with real interaction (Lightning Bolt, Journey to Nowhere, Lava Dart) and a workable 18-land mana base, even if the Eidolons and some creatures are underpowered. Deck B is an unfocused pile. Sneaky Snacker can't be cast off R/W mana and only comes back through a narrow draw-three trigger. The Tireless Tribe/Inside Out/Fling combo has few pieces and weak protection, and clunky Eidolons dilute both plans.

Deck B has a real engine. Survival of the Fittest, sac outlets (Goblin Bombardment, Phyrexian Tower, Cabal Therapy) and recursive value bodies (Squee, Symbiotic Wurm, Deranged Hermit, Karmic Guide) let Academy Rector fetch Survival or Bombardment, and the deck has an actual way to win. Deck A is a pile of unrelated pieces, with Decree of Silence, Future Sight, Deed, Fact or Fiction and Gaea's Blessing alongside almost no win conditions and Rector targets that don't justify it, and its mana is stretched across five colors for little payoff.

Deck A is a coherent Survival toolbox. Rector fetches Survival, Bombardment or Pattern, and the Bombardment and Cabal Therapy sac outlets, the Karmic Guide recursion and the Squee/Hermit/Wurm value all play together, with Birds and fetches holding up the five-colour mana. Deck B is a muddled pile: eight-mana Decree, three Gaea's Blessing, and few creatures or sac outlets to trigger Rector and Explorer. Its splashy pain-land mana base doesn't support a clear win condition.

Deck B is a real Reanimator shell: Buried Alive, Exhume, Reanimate, Animate Dead, Putrid Imp, Dark Ritual and Petals can put a 6/6 that wipes the board into play on turns 1-2. Its weak targets and the odd Utopia Trees are fixable flaws. Deck A needs a 4-mana Sneak Attack plus specific fatties in hand, and its Survival pitches have nowhere to go except a slow Genesis, so it is a clunky pile with too many moving parts.

Deck B has a real kill: Survival finds Dragon Tyrant or Nicol Bolas, and Sneak Attack puts it in with haste for a lethal or game-ending hit. Its mana dorks, 22 lands and Duress/Therapy/Fiend disruption hang together. Deck A goes through all the trouble of reanimating to land a 6/6 Bloodfire Colossus (or a Wurm) whose blast also hits itself, a poor payoff padded out with weak Rhystic Tutors.
